Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (2014)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 21.1 et seq (individuals with significant control register); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Charter of the French language, CQLR c C-11; FINTRAC guidance on beneficial ownership and politically exposed persons

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport (biographic page) for each director, officer, shareholder and individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the origin country's designated competent authority; for non-Hague Convention states, full consular legalization through the Canadian/Quebec consular mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of current residential address for each UBO and director (utility bill or regulated financial institution statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated financial institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the document originates outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / corporate registry extract for each corporate shareholder or ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or companies house in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, full consular legalization plus certified French/English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Declaration of Individual(s) with Significant Control (UBO piercing declaration under QBCA and legal publicity regime)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec notary member of the Chambre des notaires du Québec or notary equivalent in the UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization in Quebec; if executed abroad, Hague Apostille or consular legalization plus certified translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation when a representative or agent executes incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the place of signature
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization and certified French/English translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against FINTRAC guidance, Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations (SOR/2002-184), OFAC SDN List, United Nations Security Council sanctions, Canadian Special Economic Measures Act (SC 1992, c 17), United Nations Act (SC 1990, c 45), Criminal Code terrorist entity listings, and Revenu Québec/AMF administrative records. Enhanced due diligence is required for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons and close associates, high-risk jurisdictions, and non-ferrous scrap metal trade; ongoing transaction monitoring and source-of-funds documentation must be maintained.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online name research and reservation portal; where the federal CBCA route is selected, Corporations Canada NUANS Name Search and Online Filing Centre with subsequent Quebec extra-provincial registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, the adopted corporate name must have a mandatory French character; non-French names must be accompanied by a French generic descriptor or properly transliterated into Latin script, with accents and French forms preserved. The Registraire assesses distinctiveness, deception, and statutory prohibitions in both French and English name elements.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written refusal by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, the applicant may file written administrative representations for reconsideration within 30 days of the notice. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Court of Québec under the Code of Civil Procedure. A name reservation may be renewed for one additional 90-day period; any material change to the proposed name requires a new clearance application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for registered-office purposes only if a physical Quebec business address with staff, corporate records, and mail-handling capacity is maintained through an authorized registered agent. For recycled copper wire trading, a purely virtual mailbox without local operational, storage, or inspection capacity will not satisfy Revenu Québec registration, environmental oversight, or customs/bank substance expectations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-high: approximately 40% annual probability of unannounced inspection for non-ferrous scrap trading operations, driven by Ministère de l'Environnement, municipal by-law officers, police property/pawn inspections, and Revenu Québec audits. Original weight tickets, source declarations, purchase/sale records, and Quebec storage and shipment documents must be available on site.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO significant-control register preparation and filing, including individual with significant control declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent / corporate service provider / Registraire des entreprises du Québec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for legal drafting and government filing

Certified translation into French of foreign apostilled or legalized documents
Registered office in Quebec, first-year minimum commercial substance arrangement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent / serviced office provider in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for annual registered-office services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly rate for cross-border corporate and AML/CFT compliance work

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, including sections 5-7 on constitution, sections 32-38 on share capital and subscriptions, sections 104-109 on directors, and sections 119-121 on officers; Quebec Business Corporations Regulation, CQLR c. S-31.1, r. 1. The Quebec Civil Code, CQLR c. CCQ-1991, and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, also apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), administered by the Ministère de l'Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for constitution of a Québec business corporation and accompanying articles of incorporation, filed through the REQ online services or prescribed paper process
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for consideration authorized by the directors, subject to the articles, corporate law, solvency rules, and proper recording in the securities register. Quebec does not generally require incorporation capital to be deposited in a statutory escrow account. A bank account should be opened after incorporation, and share subscription funds should be paid into the corporation and documented by subscription resolutions and accounting records.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation accept the subscription by [Subscriber] for [number and class] shares for aggregate consideration of CAD [amount], payable as recorded in the securities register. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office of the Corporation be established at [full Quebec address], subject to statutory filing and municipal requirements. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name] be appointed President, [name] Secretary, and [name] Treasurer, each to hold office at the pleasure of the Board and exercise the powers assigned by law, the articles, the by-laws, and subsequent Board resolutions. The officers are authorized to execute all incorporation, banking, tax, licensing, and regulatory documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate route, name, and Quebec registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services; municipal zoning office for the proposed premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Choose a Quebec corporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act. Conduct a corporate-name search and confirm that the proposed name is not confusingly similar to an existing name or protected mark. Confirm a physical registered office in Quebec capable of receiving official service. If using a numbered corporation, reserve or accept the assigned enterprise name. Verify that the premises permit scrap storage, sorting, processing, loading, and commercial traffic under municipal zoning.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names or numbered-company preference
Registered-office address and proof of occupancy
Share structure and authorized share classes
Municipal zoning confirmation or preliminary zoning correspondence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace the proposed name, submit an amended name search, or use a numbered corporation. If the premises are incompatible with the intended activity, obtain a zoning variance, change premises, or restrict operations to activities expressly authorized by the municipality.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicant, incorporator, Quebec legal counsel, and commissioner for oaths or notary where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the application for constitution, articles, share provisions, registered-office information, first director information, and incorporator declarations. Obtain written consents from proposed directors where applicable. Execute documents electronically only where accepted by the REQ; otherwise use signed originals. Notarization is not generally required for a standard REQ incorporation, but foreign corporate signatures, powers of attorney, identity documents, and translated documents should be notarized, legalized or apostilled where required by the receiving institution.
required_dossiers: Director consents and addresses for service
Foreign corporate authority documents, if applicable
Certified French translations where documents are not accepted in English
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct incomplete signatures, inconsistent share provisions, missing director information, or deficient translations and resubmit. Preserve a revised execution package and written authority for each signatory.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation with the REQ and pay the prescribed fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online filing portal or REQ service counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the prescribed constitution application and supporting information through the REQ portal. Pay the current fee in Canadian dollars by the accepted payment method. The required fee is not denominated in United States dollars; the numeric USD field is therefore recorded as zero rather than presenting an unreliable exchange-rate conversion. Retain the filing receipt, transaction number, submitted documents, and any name approval evidence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the REQ portal within the stated cure period, correct the queried item, pay any additional prescribed fee, and resubmit. If refused, request written reasons, file a corrected application, or seek administrative review and legal advice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain proof of constitution and complete enterprise registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the certificate or confirmation of constitution, enterprise number, Québec enterprise number, filed articles, and registry extract. Confirm the legal name, registered office, directors, activity codes, and declared business activities. File any required initial declaration or information update under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Establish procedures for annual updating, annual declarations, beneficial-owner information, and changes of directors or address.
required_dossiers: Québec enterprise number and registry extract
Initial declaration or required registry update
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a correction or update with the REQ if registry information is inaccurate. Rectify late or omitted filings promptly and assess any late fees, penalties, or reinstatement requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organize corporate governance and issue shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors, corporate records office, and Quebec corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first directors' meeting or execute unanimous written resolutions. Adopt by-laws, approve the registered office, appoint officers, approve banking authorities, authorize tax registrations, approve the business plan, and accept share subscriptions. Record consideration received, issue certificates or electronic ownership records, update the securities register, maintain the register of directors and shareholders, and prepare a corporate minute book.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Pass ratifying resolutions, correct the securities register, obtain missing consents, and document any deficient consideration or authority. Do not issue shares contrary to the articles, solvency requirements, or shareholder rights.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax, payroll, import, and cross-border trade accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Revenu Québec, Canada Border Services Agency, and Québec Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a CRA business number and register applicable GST/HST, payroll, and corporate income tax accounts. Register for Québec sales tax, employer source deductions, and Québec income tax with Revenu Québec. Obtain a CBSA import-export RM account and CARM registration before importing or exporting commercial scrap. Register with CNESST as an employer when required and establish payroll, workplace-safety, and recordkeeping controls.
required_dossiers: Certificate of constitution and enterprise numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct account applications, provide additional identity or ownership evidence, and respond to CRA, Revenu Québec, CBSA, or CNESST queries. Do not import or export regulated goods before required account activation and customs compliance review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure industrial, environmental, municipal, and fire approvals before operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Québec Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs; municipality; Régie du bâtiment du Québec; local fire-service authority; CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Define the actual activity boundary: brokerage, storage, transshipment, sorting, shredding, baling, processing, or disposal. Obtain written environmental and zoning determinations before receiving scrap. Apply for any authorization required under the Environment Quality Act and the Regulation respecting the regulatory framework applying to activities under the Environment Quality Act. Obtain building, occupancy, fire, electrical, mechanical, and construction approvals for the facility and implement workplace controls.
required_dossiers: Inventory and classification of incoming and outgoing scrap
Environmental screening and emissions or discharge calculations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to technical information requests, amend the process description, obtain a project-specific authorization, or discontinue the unapproved activity. Appeal or seek review only through the procedure and deadlines stated in the applicable decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Québec Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs for environmental authorizations; the municipality for zoning and occupancy; and the Régie du bâtiment du Québec for regulated construction and building systems. Quebec has no single general manufacturing licence for all scrap-metal businesses.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Authorization under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2, including an authorization under section 22 or another project-specific authorization required by the Regulation respecting the regulatory framework applying to activities under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2, r. 17.1. Municipal occupancy and zoning authorization is separately required. Scrap storage, sorting, shredding, processing, or transfer activities must be classified by the competent authorities before commencement.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs du Québec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-specific screening; generally no automatic full provincial EIA solely because of ordinary copper-scrap trading, storage, or processing, but an environmental authorization, declaration of conformity, exemption, or full assessment may apply depending on quantities, equipment, emissions, discharge, contaminated materials, water impacts, and site characteristics.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No single sector-wide threshold applies to every facility. The authorization or declaration controls wastewater, stormwater, dust, noise, VOCs, particulate matter, contaminated soil, and residual materials. Applicable requirements arise under the Environment Quality Act, the Regulation respecting the regulatory framework applying to activities under the Environment Quality Act, the Regulation respecting hazardous materials, municipal sewer bylaws, and federal requirements under CEPA where applicable. Copper-bearing or contaminated residuals must be characterized, stored in compatible and contained areas, tracked, and transferred only to authorized recipients. Spill prevention, dust suppression, stormwater control, and documented waste manifests or equivalent records are required where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal occupancy and fire-prevention approval before use of the premises, including fire-separation, extinguishing systems, emergency access, electrical safety, and combustible-load review. Obtain building, structural, equipment, and alteration permits through the municipality and, where applicable, the Régie du bâtiment du Québec. Complete structural load and floor-capacity assessments for scrap storage, racks, compactors, shredders, and mobile equipment. Register with CNESST when required and implement Québec occupational-health controls for machine guarding, lockout/tagout, noise, dust, traffic segregation, PPE, training, incident reporting, and emergency response.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and corporate income tax; Revenu Québec for Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and Quebec corporate income tax. Primary portals: CRA 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec 'ClicSÉQUR Affaires' (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/services-en-ligne/cles/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from CRA, then add program account identifiers: GST/HST, corporate income tax, payroll, and an import/export (RM) account. A non-resident may apply directly without Canadian incorporation; a Canadian representative or tax agent may be authorized. After federal registration, the entity must separately register with Revenu Québec if it carries on taxable activities in Quebec; Revenu Québec assigns a QST number and an enterprise number, using the federal BN where applicable. Registration as a non-resident registrant requires proof of foreign legal existence, registered address in Canada and/or a designated representative for service, and details of Canadian business operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists under Canadian law. A Quebec business corporation is always a separate taxpayer at both federal and provincial levels. Limited elections potentially applicable in cross-border scenarios include: the Income Tax Act section 216 election for non-resident income tax filing with respect to Canadian-source rents/royalties, and treaty-based tie-breaker determinations regarding residence for a corporation incorporated in Canada but managed outside Canada. No hybrid mismatch election is available the exporter can use to alter entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) - invoice-credit value-added tax systems administered by CRA and Revenu Québec, respectively.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of cumulative taxable supplies (before expenses) for both GST/HST and QST small-supplier thresholds; once exceeded, registration is mandatory within 30 days for GST/HST and within the prescribed period for QST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently impose a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate for B2B invoices. Registered suppliers must retain invoices in an audit-trail format acceptable to CRA and Revenu Québec. GST/HST returns must be filed electronically through GST/HST NETFILE once required, and QST returns through Services en ligne Revenu Québec. B2B e-invoicing may be transacted through EDI/PEPPOL but is not mandatory. For exports, customs declarations must be transmitted electronically to the CBSA through CARM-compatible EDI/API channels or its portal; no revenue-authority 'digital stamp' is affixed to invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST and QST registrant may zero-rate export supplies of tangible personal property, including shredded copper scrap and non-ferrous metal waste, under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act and the corresponding QST rules, provided the property is shipped or delivered by the supplier to a recipient outside Canada, or to a non-resident recipient, and is exported as soon as is reasonably possible after the supply is made. The supplier must retain proof of export and must not use the goods in Canada before export. The zero-rating applies regardless of whether the foreign purchaser is registered for GST/HST or QST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration, Canada Customs Export Declaration (CCECD), or equivalent CARM/EDI export manifest record
Bill of lading / multimodal transport document showing Canadian exporter and overseas consignee
Weight ticket, scale report, and assay or grade certificate for shredded copper scrap
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT MT103 credit advice, or bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating where the exporter fails to provide contemporaneous documentary proof of export. If zero-rating is denied, the exporter is liable for unreported GST/HST and QST on the deemed taxable supply, plus interest and late-filing penalties, with a retrospective reassessment normally limited to four years, extended to six or more years in cases of negligence or misrepresentation. Additional civil penalties apply under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec fiscal statutes for false statements, omissions, or wilful evasion, including penalties of up to 25% of the tax evaded and, for indictable offences, fines and imprisonment. Exporters involved in fraud may also lose refunds, be added to non-compliant registrant lists, and face customs penalties under CBSA legislation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Canada maintains no single foreign exchange administration; policy responsibility rests with the Bank of Canada, prudential bank supervision with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), AML/ATF supervision with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), and export documentation with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada operates under full current-account and capital-account convertibility with no exchange-control statute; the former Exchange Control Act has been repealed and the Canadian dollar is freely convertible. Trade payments, service payments, dividends, interest, royalties, equity injections and intercompany loans may flow without central-bank approval or licence. The only practical remittance hurdles are: (i) non-resident withholding taxes under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada), normally 25% reduced by treaty, with parallel Quebec withholding under the Taxation Act (Quebec); (ii) FINTRAC reporting of international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; (iii) enhanced source-of-funds verification imposed by Schedule I banks on non-resident remitters; and (iv) the requirement that profit remittances be supported by board resolutions, audited financial statements and proof of arm's-length pricing, particularly where a Quebec recycled-scrap exporter distributes to a foreign parent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio and no repatriation deadline. Exporters may freely retain, hedge and disburse foreign currency receipts. Compliance anchors are instead documentary and statistical: (i) each export shipment over CAD 2,000 must be reported to CBSA through the CARM portal / B13A export declaration, and the associated transaction number should be retained as underlying-trade evidence; (ii) international EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more are reportable to FINTRAC; and (iii) an export certificate, commercial invoice and bills of lading must evidence the zero-rated GST/HST and QST treatment of qualifying exported copper scrap, which in turn forms part of the banking audit trail for outbound trade settlements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary treasury usage. Canada does not recognise the EU electronic-money-institution (EMI) licence; an entity accepting retail deposits is either a regulated bank (Schedule I/II) or a money-service business registered with FINTRAC, and payment-service providers must additionally register under the Retail Payment Activities Act with the Bank of Canada. Offshore digital EMIs cannot issue or confirm documentary letters of credit, do not provide CDIC-insured deposit accounts, and commonly prohibit scrap-metal trade flows in their terms. They are acceptable only as a secondary collection gateway for small pre-shipment deposits, never as the exclusive settlement rail for documentary LC-backed copper wire exports.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Federal PCMLTFA rules permit remote identity verification such as dual-process or credit-bureau matching, so in-person presence is not statutorily mandatory; however, Tier-1 Schedule I banks treat scrap-metal merchant wholesaling as an enhanced-risk sector and a Quebec corporation with non-resident UBOs as elevated risk. In practice, at least one director or authorized senior officer must attend a physical branch interview at the Montreal or Quebec City business banking centre for signature verification and e-signing of the mandate; alternatively, certain banks (National Bank, RBC, BMO) may accept a notarised remote opening package followed by a live video identity check. TD, CIBC and Scotiabank generally require physical attendance of a director for this industry profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry red flag: scrap-metal and recycled-commodity wholesaling is recognised by FINTRAC as a money-laundering-vulnerable sector, with risks of cash recycling, mispricing of commodity value and stolen-material provenance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defence bundle: Quebec Registraire des entreprises attestation and NEQ registration; certificate of incorporation and by-laws; written AML/ATF policy and designated compliance officer; complete customer and supplier KYB files with corporate extracts; chain-of-custody documentation per shipment (signed purchase orders, scale weight tickets, container numbers, bills of lading, CBSA B13A export records); assay or copper-content certificates where available; and two years of reviewed or audited financial statements evidencing commercial substance and liquidity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership or UBO citizenship/tax residency in a high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO register disclosing the full 100% ownership chain (name, date of birth, address, nationality, ownership percentage); passport and proof of residential address; source-of-wealth statement supported by asset sale agreements, operating business records or loan/gift instruments; notarised bank reference from the UBO's home-country bank; trust deed or share register where a trust or nominee appears; and a shareholder undertaking confirming no bearer shares or undisclosed nominee arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sudden inbound cross-border capital injection (equity or shareholder loan) not matched by existing business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed share-subscription resolution or intercompany loan agreement; corporate minutes; source-of-funds evidence comprising upstream bank statements showing the remitter held the funds in its own account; CRA and Revenu Quebec tax clearance where available; a first-year business plan with forecast copper-wire tonnage and buyer contracts; and a written 90-day holding undertaking before outbound disbursement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment instructions, payments routed through high-risk jurisdictions, or correspondent ghost-account structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contracts with Incoterms and exact beneficiary banking details; pro-forma and final commercial invoices; transport documents (bills of lading, pre-shipment inspection certificate, insurance certificates); a written covenant that cash payments will not exceed the FINTRAC CAD 10,000 reporting threshold; strict segregation of collection and disbursement accounts; and counterparty KYB confirmations for European or North American off-takers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital from a non-resident shareholder should be remitted by SWIFT MT103 with ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' for equity injection, 'LOAN' for shareholder debt, or 'TRAA' for goods pre-payment, into the Quebec corporation's CAD/USD operating account at the chosen Schedule I bank. No Bank of Canada approval or exchange-control form is required. Prior to the transfer, the Canadian receiving bank should receive a funds pre-advice package: NEQ registration, directors' resolution authorising the injection, UBO and source-of-funds evidence. The wire must state the remitter's full legal name, the corporation's full legal name and NEQ number, and the trip's economic purpose to avoid sanctions-policy false positives. FINTRAC EFT reporting applies to international transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. For inbound direct investment, Statistics Canada inward investment reporting thresholds apply; the injection must be documented in a CBCA/Quebec share register and, where applicable, registered with the Registraire des entreprises within the statutory period. Capital should be parked in a dedicated capital escrow sub-account for at least 90 days before application to trade disbursements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement to overseas scrap suppliers and tolling partners uses three primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for telegraphic payments, using purpose codes 'TRAA' or 'GDSO', matched against commercial invoices, weight lists and bills of lading retained as a transaction audit file; (ii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued by the Canadian bank via SWIFT MT700, typically confirmed by a top-tier foreign bank, with the document schedule comprising commercial invoice, full set of clean-on-board ocean bills of lading, weight/assay certificate, certificate of origin and pre-shipment inspection certificate; and (iii) domestic CAD settlement through Payments Canada's Lynx real-time gross settlement system or the Automated Clearing Settlement System, with USD cleared through the Canadian bank's correspondent account and Fedwire. All outbound disbursements above CAD 10,000 trigger FINTRAC EFT reports and the bank's enhanced transaction monitoring, requiring production of underlying commercial paper within five business days of any transaction-call for documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/CAD outright FX forwards (standard tenor 1–24 months) executed with a Canadian Schedule I bank under an ISDA Master Agreement or short-form FX confirmation
USD/CAD Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — contractually permissible under Canadian law, though the deep deliverable USD/CAD market makes deliverable forwards the preferred mechanism
USD/CAD cross-currency swaps for matched long-term trade payables and capital-repatriation structural hedging
Plain-vanilla USD/CAD FX options and zero-cost collars for budget-rate protection on scrap-copper settlements
LME copper futures and forwards executed through a licensed commodity broker, maintained as a separate price-risk book from the FX hedging programme

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs escalating administrative penalties; after 3 consecutive years of non-filing, the enterprise may be struck off and dissolved by the registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for 1 year may trigger the Director's power to dissolve the corporation; continued default exposes the corporation to summary offence fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Federal Corporate Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month (max 12 months) and daily interest; failure to file may result in prosecution and hypothecs on assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CO-17 Quebec Corporate Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: 5% of balance owed plus 1% per month (max 12 months); interest accrues on unpaid amounts; non-filing may lead to a warrant of execution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (if annual remitter election applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 3 months after fiscal year-end for annual filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: 5% of net amount due plus 1% per month (max 12 months); interest and potential cancellation of annual election.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private corporations under CBCA/QBCA are exempt from mandatory audit if all shareholders (unanimous consent) waive the auditor requirement. An audit is mandatory for public reporting issuers and distributing corporations. Individual shareholders holding at least 5% of issued voting shares may requisition an independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations. Cross-border traders with external financing or parent guarantees may be required by lenders to adopt IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, during the statutory annual filing, the corporation must confirm that its Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) is up-to-date and accurately reflects all direct and indirect share transfers and ownership changes. Any change in significant control must be recorded in the ISC register within 15 days of the corporation becoming aware. Annual filing under CBCA/QBCA includes a certification that the ISC register has been updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,000 - 25,000 USD depending on volume of transactions and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal + Quebec general rate (15.0% federal + 11.5% provincial)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) 9% federal / 3.2% Quebec on first CAD 500,000 active business income is restricted to Canadian-controlled private corporations and is unavailable where control is non-resident; general rate reduction to 13% applies only to manufacturing/processing profits; no specific tax holiday for scrap-metal trading.
